title: Consistency, Queues & Idempotency
summary: Prevent double-charging, lost events, stuck workers, and oversold inventory under failures.
body:
Distributed systems fail partially: networks drop acknowledgements, workers crash mid-job, and downstream APIs stall. Use explicit coordination primitives wherever correctness matters.

## At-least-once queues + idempotency
True end-to-end 'exactly-once' across external side effects does not exist; build effectively-once behavior from two halves:
- Producer durability: write domain changes and outbound events atomically in one local DB transaction (`Transactional Outbox`), then relay to the queue.
- Consumer idempotency: require a deterministic `idempotency_key` or `event_id` recorded with a unique constraint so retries become safe no-ops.

## Contention, holds, and leases
- Preventing double-sell (tickets, local inventory): use row-level locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`), atomic conditional updates (`UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'AVAILABLE'`), or optimistic `version` checks.
- Temporary holds: transition inventory to `HELD` with an explicit `expires_at` timestamp during payment, reclaiming expired holds lazily or via background sweepers.
- Worker leases and fencing: assign long-running tasks a visibility timeout renewed by heartbeats plus a monotonic fencing token so a zombie worker delayed by GC cannot overwrite newer results.

## Failure isolation
- Separate critical queues (password resets, interactive code runs) from bulk queues (campaigns, contest batches).
- Retry transient errors with exponential backoff + jitter, cap attempts into a Dead-Letter Queue (`DLQ`), and trip per-destination circuit breakers on broken webhooks or providers.
